newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch monitors withdraw advance team from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Dutch monitors withdraw advance team from Iraq.

text.p: Dutch industrial inspectors Saybolt have withdrawn an advance team of three from Baghdad in the light of this week's Iraqi crisis and with the oil-for-food deal looking more distant, a spokesman said.
"It could be months before the deal goes ahead, so we feel it doesn't make sense to keep them there. I believe they left this morning," the spokesman told Reuters.
The two technicians and one manager had been in Baghdad for four to five days, in advance of 11 other monitors Saybolt was to send.

The U.N./Iraqi oil-for-food deal was to have allowed Iraq to export oil -- $2 billion worth over six months -- for the first time since August 1990. Saybolt were appointed by the United Nations as monitors of the Iraqi oil exports.
On Sunday, U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali postponed plans to implement the deal on safety fears after Iraqi troops entered Kurdish areas in northern Iraq.
